many many feature requests.

This PR is now in theory in a mergeable state (although it should not be merged right now). **Code review** would be very much appreciated, please. All major changes have been made. The only changes now will be bug fixes, optimization improvements, or renaming and refactoring things. 

**When reviewing, click on File Filter, and deselect all extensions apart from .cpp and .h**. Everything else is mtest/ui files, and doesn't need reviewing (unless of course you really want to).

You can experience this PR using S. Christian's test soundfont, [downloadable here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Cq3TYJofteh720UW88Wbq_WoJkeW5xFw/view?usp=sharing). In the mixer, set an instrument's patch to 'CC2 expression'.

Most of the significant work (i.e. not just adding properties, changing inspector files etc.) is in **rendermidi.cpp**. This file is hidden by default, since the diff is so large. Please make sure, if reviewing, that you do not accidently skip over it.

For reference, [here is the proposal post](https://musescore.org/en/node/280281). Note that this PR does not follow the proposal completely, and instead only uses parts of it.

Wording of any new UI elements is open to change, so feel free to suggest better names for things. I'd rather keep internal names the same as they are now, though.

This also adds a new demo, which demonstrates all of this PR's capabilities (except for different interpolation methods).

## Key features

- Hairpins crescendo and diminuendo smoothly between dynamics
  - Instruments that cannot do this, by default, have this disabled. It is editable in the Staff properties dialogue
  - Hairpin interpolation methods are selectable, from linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in and out, and exponential.
- Fortepianos and, in fact, *all* dynamics can have 'velocity change' assigned to them. By default, this is only set for fortepianos and all variants of them, but it is available for all dynamics.
  - The speed at which this velocity change happens is editable in the inspector. Internally, it is an enum, `Ms::Dynamic::Speed`.
- Articulations are handled with single-note dynamics. After holding the initial velocity for some ticks, the note will 'drop off' back down to its normal velocity.
- Both fortepianos and articulations integrate seamlessly, in theory and so far in practice, with hairpins
- Advanced dynamics settings, and the ability to disable this completely and revert to the current method, are in the synthesizer. Another new setting also provides compatability with soundfonts that don't use CC2, instead using CC1, 4, or 11.

### Optimization
The code is not fully optimized yet, but is still fairly optimized. Please point out ways of making it more so.

So, that's it really. Enjoy!

Sample score:

[Audio is downloadable/viewable here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uk0iR6fJqfmUwmzu9iitFQYSNClJTeK_/view?usp=sharing).
